subject: Econ alignment, POC success criteria & action agenda
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Kayla Morgan <kayla.morgan@brightscale.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Econ alignment, POC success criteria & action agenda

Kayla — great to meet you and Ian earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so BrightScale can share internally. TL;DR: economic buyer is confirmed (Ian), security wants a short questionnaire + evidence, procurement needs initial SOW/estimate and standard T&Cs.

Key notes from the call:
- Primary objectives: validate latency at 95th < 200ms for 512-token requests, and 2x cost reduction vs current provider for inference at 100k tokens/day.
- POC scope: 2-week controlled POC against production-like traffic (500 concurrent requests peak), integration of prefix caching and a single model variant.
- Success criteria (we agreed on):
  1) 95th percentile latency < 200ms for 95% of test windows
  2) <= 1.5x of current error rate on test prompts
  3) Clear telemetry surfaced in Console with token-level cost breakdown
- Economic buyer: Ian Chu (confirmed).
- Security/Legal asks: standard SOC2 evidence, data retention policy, and the short questionnaire we discussed.
- Procurement: will want a draft SOW + ballpark pricing and renewal cadence.

Proposed mutual action agenda (draft) — keyed to the week-by-week POC we recommended:
Week 0 (this week): exchange security questionnaire + sign NDA if needed. Redwood to provide SOW draft and staging credentials.
Week 1: Integration + smoke tests (we provide onboarding playbook and a short runbook).
Week 2: Load test + joint acceptance run; Redwood provides cost/latency report and tuning.
Close: Decision meeting with Ian, procurement sign-off or request for extended trial.

Ask from BrightScale this week (can you confirm by Wed?):
- Security contact name + email to send the questionnaire to (we'll attach the questionnaire).
- Preferred procurement contact and any PO template or legal checklist.
- Any absolute deal-breaker requirements we should be aware of (e.g., data residency, encryption at rest keys with specific KMS).

Attachments: security_questionnaire.pdf (short form), example SOW placeholder (we'll send a first pass after you confirm procurement contact).

Thanks — I looped Marcus on technical integration and Neha on legal/compliance for visibility. Will follow up with a first-pass SOW once you confirm procurement contact.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priym.das@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Kayla Morgan <kayla.morgan@brightscale.com>

Cc: Ian Chu <ian.chu@brightscale.com>, Procurement <procure@brightscale.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Econ alignment, POC success criteria & action agenda

Priyom — thanks for the clear recap. Couple quick items from our side:

1) Security contact: please send the questionnaire to Julia Park (julia.park@brightscale.com), our Sr. InfoSec. She requested we include evidence for data deletion logs and KV cache isolation.
2) Procurement: procurement@brightscale.com (looping Shaun in the procurement alias). Shaun will own SOW review and PO routing.
3) Timeline: the team prefers the POC to run in early November (Nov 2 start) due to QA calendar — is that workable?
4) Success criteria tweak: Ian asked that latency target be captured at 95th for both cold and warmed KV-cache runs (so we understand cache impact).

Also attaching a redline checklist of legal terms they typically require (see inline). We expect a standard master services agreement review; they want to limit data retention to 90 days for raw logs unless otherwise agreed.

We are fine with your proposed weeks but will confirm exact start date after procurement signs off. Please send the SOW and the questionnaire to Julia, cc'ing procurement.

Best,
Kayla
VP, Product Partnerships | BrightScale
kayla.morgan@brightscale.com

Internal note — forwarding Kayla's reply. Short list of actions for us: 

Neha: Julia asked for evidence on data deletion logs and KV cache isolation. Can we pull the template SOC2 artifact and a short note on cache partitioning? Also need guidance on the 90-day retention ask and whether we need an exception or can commit it in SOW.
Marcus: Kayla wants the latency split for cold vs warmed cache at 95th. Can you prepare a short test plan and a runbook for the POC that includes cache warm-up steps and the exact telemetry we will collect?

I'll prepare the draft SOW and send to procurement@brightscale.com and Julia after we have the security artifacts. Target: send SOW + questionnaire by Fri EOD (23 Oct).

Thanks — Priyom

Subject: SOW + questionnaire (draft) and proposed POC start dates — action needed

Kayla / Julia / Shaun — attaching the draft SOW (redwood-poc-sow-v1.docx) and the filled security_questionnaire.pdf. Summary of changes vs our call:
- POC start window options: Nov 2 or Nov 9 (BrightScale choose and confirm).
- We explicitly call out two latency measurements: cold-cache 95th and warmed-cache 95th, plus token-level cost report.
- Data retention: we proposed 90-day raw log retention with option to extend under a data addendum — flagged for your legal.
- Deliverables: onboarding runbook, test plan, telemetry dashboard access, one joint acceptance report at POC close.

Action items for this thread (please reply inline where possible):
1) BrightScale: confirm POC start date (Nov 2 or Nov 9) and procurement contact for SOW signatures.
2) Julia: confirm whether the attached questionnaire is sufficient or list any remaining evidence items; if you need a SOC2 export, we'll schedule a secure share.
3) Procurement: please confirm PO process (approx timeline) and any contract redlines we should expect.

If there are any non-starters in the SOW language, flag them and we'll iterate quickly — aim is to keep the POC scope narrow and measurable.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Best,
